description: The Cairo Agreement formally grants Palestinians the right to launch operations from Lebanese soil following clashes between Palestinian forces and the Lebanese army. It enables the growth of a Palestinian state-within-a-state in the south.
Civil war in Jordan results in the expulsion of PLO forces, accelerating their consolidation in southern Lebanon. This significantly increases cross-border tensions with Israel.
Ayn al-Rummana bus ambush by Phalangists: Lebanese Civil War begins.
Fall of Tal al-Zat'ar after 53-day siege: approximately 3,000 killed; PLO position in Lebanon significantly weakened.

A peace agreement for Lebanon brokered by six Arab leaders during a summit in Saudi Arabia to end the ongoing Lebanese Civil War. Saw the deployment of an Arab League Peacekeeping Force (the Arab Deterrent Force) to end hostilities and keep the peace.

Israel invades and occupies South Lebanon up to the Litani River in response to PLO cross-border attacks. The operation marks the beginning of prolonged Israeli military engagement in Lebanese territory.
UNSCR 425/426: UNIFIL established with initial six-month mandate. The mission is mandated to confirm withdrawal, restore peace, and assist Lebanon in reasserting authority in the south.

event: First UNIFIL troops deploy to south Lebanon
description: First UNIFIL troops deploy to south Lebanon. The force begins operating in an area still contested between Israeli forces and armed Palestinian groups.
Israel completes formal withdrawal but transfers positions to SLA (Haddad forces), not UNIFIL — first major mandate failure.

Israel withdraws its forces under US pressure but transfers the border zone to the right-wing South Lebanon Army (SLA) auxiliary. Israel is widely regarded as retaining effective control, leading to repeated renewal of UNIFIL's mandate.

Intensifying cross-border exchanges between the PLO and Israel prompt US Ambassador Philip Habib to broker a ceasefire. The agreement holds temporarily but is later used by Israel as a pretext for the 1982 invasion.

Following the wounding of Israeli Ambassador Argov in London by Abu Nidal gunmen (Iraqi-linked, not PLO), Israel launches its second invasion of Lebanon, advancing as far as Beirut. The invasion dramatically expands Israel's occupation and reshapes the Lebanese political landscape. US vetoes UNSC expansion of mandate. Israeli invasion reaches Beirut; UNIFIL unable to block advance; contingents attempt symbolic but ineffective resistance.
Sabra and Shatila massacre: approximately 1,000+ killed by Phalangist forces with Israeli facilitation.
Israel pulls back from the Beirut region but retains occupation of the entire south up to the Awwali River north of Sidon. Full occupation of the south continues for a further three years.
A US-brokered accord between Israel and Lebanon is signed but quickly collapses. Syria, whose consent was not sought, effectively vetoes the agreement.

Israeli forces violate the sanctity of Ashura, prompting senior Sunni and Shia clerics to issue a fatwa declaring a defensive jihad against the occupation. The incident radicalises previously moderate religious figures in the region.
A Hezbollah-linked suicide bombing destroys the US Marine barracks in Beirut, killing over 240 Marines. The attack is one of the deadliest single-day losses for the US military since World War II.
Israeli cabinet approves staged withdrawal; residual 'security zone' established under SLA/Lahad command.

Hezbollah publishes its founding ideological manifesto, the 'Open Letter,' formally articulating its goals, identity, and resistance posture. The document establishes the organisation's ideological framework for decades to come.

1985 to 1988. Amal launches a siege of Palestinian refugee camps in Beirut and the south, initiating the so-called 'War of the Camps.' The conflict lasts approximately two years and deepens sectarian and factional divisions.

IDF completes third-stage withdrawal; post-1985 security zone consolidated and expanded under SLA/Lahad. Israel retains a 10–20 km 'security belt' along the border, including a salient around Jizzin — roughly 10% of Lebanese territory. The SLA continues to administer the zone under Israeli direction.

Armed clashes break out between Amal and Hezbollah, reflecting growing competition for Shia political and military dominance in Lebanon. The conflict is eventually resolved by the 1990 Damascus Accord.

event: Kidnapping of Lt. Col. William Higgins
description: Lt. Col. William Higgins, serving with the UN Observer Group Lebanon, is kidnapped by the Amal splinter group 'Believer's Resistance' led by Mustafa Dirani, with suspected Hezbollah sympathies. Higgins is later killed; responsibility is attributed to the 'Revolutionary Justice Organization.'

The Ta'if Agreement ends Lebanon's civil war and mandates disarmament of all militias including Amal. Amal's entry into formal politics causes its militant cadres to migrate toward Hezbollah, strengthening the latter.
Iran and Syria sponsor the Damascus Accord, ending two years of armed hostilities between Amal and Hezbollah. The agreement consolidates Hezbollah's position as the dominant Shia armed movement.
Hezbollah participates in Lebanese parliamentary elections for the first time, winning 12 seats — strategic pivot to political actor.

Israel launches Operation Accountability on 25 July, targeting Hezbollah bases north of the security zone with the aim of curtailing guerrilla operations. A US-brokered ceasefire is reached on 31 July through Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
Qana massacre: IDF shells UNIFIL Fijian HQ sheltering ~800 civilians; 106 killed including 52 children; Van Kappen investigation initiated but suppressed.
Israeli Operation Grapes of Wrath.
Israel-Hezbollah Document of Understanding establishes informal rules of the game.

Former Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Subhi Tufayli launches a populist initiative demanding jobs, crop subsidies, free education, utilities, and state pensions for resistance fighters. The move represents a direct challenge to both Hezbollah's leadership and state authority.

After months of defiance, Tufayli attempts to disrupt Hezbollah's Jerusalem Day commemoration in Baalbek and is expelled from the organisation within 24 hours. The episode underscores Hezbollah's intolerance of internal dissent.

event: Lebanon rejects participation in Blue Line demarcation
description: Lebanon refuses to participate in informal UN Blue Line demarcation process — an early signal of the state's ambivalent attitude toward boundary formalization.

event: Israeli full withdrawal from south Lebanon
description: Israel withdraws completely from south Lebanon and the SLA is disbanded, ending 22 years of occupation. UNIFIL remains deployed as the Lebanese government has still not restored effective authority over the area.

event: Three IDF soldiers kidnapped at Shab'a Farms
description: Three IDF soldiers kidnapped at Shab'a Farms — first major post-withdrawal test of the 'rules of the game.'
UN scales down UNIFIL; Finland and Ireland withdraw.

event: First local elections in south Lebanon in 38 years
description: First local elections in south Lebanon in 38 years; Amal-Hezbollah electoral pact wins 90 of 115 municipal councils.
Mt. Dov escalation; Iranian FM Kharazi urges Hezbollah restraint in Beirut — documents Iranian dual restraint role.
IAF strikes Syrian territory (Palestinian camp near Damascus) — first such strike in 30 years; tests 'rules of the game' threshold.

UNSC calls for the withdrawal of all foreign forces from Lebanon and the dismantling of all militias. The resolution is widely understood as targeting both Syrian presence (25k troops) and Hezbollah's armed wing.

Syria completes its military withdrawal from Lebanon following domestic and international pressure in the wake of the Hariri assassination. The withdrawal ends nearly three decades of Syrian military presence.
Finland and Ireland return to UNIFIL at UN request as joint Finnish/Irish Battalion.

Israel launches a major military campaign against Lebanon primarily targeting Hezbollah, following the capture of two Israeli soldiers. The war results in UNSC Resolution 1701 and a significantly expanded UNIFIL mandate.

Newly elected Italian PM Romano Prodi co-chairs a peace conference in Rome with the US, calling for an ad-hoc peacekeeping mission in Lebanon and signalling Italy's readiness to contribute troops. The conference foreshadows the expanded UNIFIL mandate under Resolution 1701.
UNSC Resolution 1701 adopted; UNIFIL reinforced to up to 15,000 troops with European TCC backbone.
Italy provides interim naval vessel to enable Israeli sea blockade lift; Interim MTF formed.

event: Spanish UNIFIL peacekeepers killed near al-Khiyam
description: Six soldiers of the Spanish UNIFIL battalion are killed by a vehicle-borne IED near the Shia village of al-Khiyam. The attack is one of the deadliest against UNIFIL since the mission's expansion in 2006.
Italian General Graziano assumes UNIFIL Force Command (until Jan 2010).

event: Six Spanish UNIFIL soldiers killed by VBIED near al-Khiyam
description: Six Spanish UNIFIL soldiers killed by VBIED near al-Khiyam — deadliest single attack on UNIFIL II.
Israeli-Hezbollah prisoner exchange mediated by German diplomat Gerhard Conrad — significant German bilateral contribution.

President Michel Suleiman convenes a national dialogue process addressing core sovereignty and disarmament questions, including Hezbollah's weapons. The dialogue reflects ongoing Lebanese political paralysis over the resistance arms issue.
LAF-IDF clash near Blue Line; UNIFIL Indonesian contingent unable to de-escalate.

event: LAF declares Blue Line a closed military zone
description: LAF, coordinating with UNIFIL, declares Blue Line area a closed military zone during Nakba Day protests; prevents cross-border civilian incursion.

The European Union designates Hezbollah's military wing as a terrorist organisation, following years of debate among member states. The designation complicates UNIFIL's liaison arrangements with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, given that several major TCCs are EU members.
Hezbollah ATGM attack kills two IDF soldiers near Shebaa Farms; Israeli return fire kills one Spanish UNIFIL member.

event: Estonia joins Finnish contingent in UNIFIL
description: Estonia joins Finnish contingent as platoon-sized unit in UNIFIL Western Sector.
Hezbollah fighters deliberately photographed near UNIFIL headquarters during a scheduled Blue Line liaison tour — documented information operation against both UNIFIL and LAF.

event: Hezbollah attacks Jabhat al-Nusra in Arsal
description: Hezbollah launches unilateral military operation against Jabhat al-Nusra in Arsal border area; LAF adopts strict deconfliction posture; ceasefire declared 27 July.
SCR 2373 adopted; demands more prompt and detailed reporting on 1701 violations from UNIFIL.

event: President Aoun defends Hezbollah's right to maintain weapons
description: President Aoun publicly declares Hezbollah weapons 'a principal element of Lebanon's defense' — formally legitimizes violation of SCR 1701 disarmament provisions.

event: First UNIFIL periodic report since SCR 2373
description: First UNIFIL periodic report following SCR 2373 confirms no 'verified findings' at any suspected Hezbollah sites despite enhanced monitoring requirements.

event: UNIFIL patrol attacked near Majdal Zoun
description: UNIFIL patrol attacked near Majdal Zoun by approximately 20 armed activists; Lebanese investigation contradicts UN findings; perpetrators unprosecuted as of 2019.
IDF Operation Northern Shield begins; exposes six Hezbollah cross-border attack tunnels crossing the Blue Line into Israel; concludes 13 Jan 2019.
UN observers witness concrete flowing from a Lebanese chicken coop into a tunnel crossing the Blue Line — first irrefutable physical proof of tunnel infrastructure.

event: UNIFIL-LAF MOU on de-mining south of Litani
description: UNIFIL-LAF MOU signed on de-mining south of Litani.
Beirut port explosion: 218 killed, 7,000+ injured; fundamentally redirects international attention from southern Lebanon security.
SCR 2539 adopted; UNIFIL force ceiling reduced from 15,000 to 13,000; mandate renewed for one year without substantive change.
Launch of formal Lebanon-Israel maritime border negotiations under US mediation.
Spanish General Major General Aroldo Lázaro Sáenz assumes command of UNIFIL mission.
Hezbollah opens fire across Blue Line in solidarity with Gaza; south Lebanon war resumes.
Israeli escalation; assassination of Nasrallah and Hezbollah leadership; ground invasion of south Lebanon.
Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire; Quintet Enforcement Committee (US, France, Israel, Lebanon, UNIFIL) established, replaces Trilateral Military Committee.
Fall of Assad regime; Hezbollah loses Syrian overland resupply route to Iran, a significant strategic setback.
12-day US-Israeli war on Iran (13–24 Jun 2025); Hezbollah stays out, preserving its forces but taking a significant legitimacy hit domestically.
Italian Major General Diodato Abagnara assumes Force Commander role.
SCR 2790 adopted; final UNIFIL mandate renewal to 31 December 2026, driven primarily by US pressure.
Quintet monitoring mechanism collapses; Israel stops attending meetings; no functional de-escalation mechanism remains.

Hezbollah fires rockets in Israel following US assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei; Israel applies 'Gaza model': mass displacement, razing of border villages, deep buffer zone to Litani. Lebanese government issues unprecedented formal ban on Hezbollah military activity.
